name: Sen. Kelly Loeffler

summary.text: Kelly Loeffler served as a U.S. Senator from Georgia in 2020. After she and her husband sold between $1.2 million and $3.1 million in stock following a closed-door Senate coronavirus briefing on January 24, 2020, the Justice Department opened and, in May 2020, closed an investigation, and on June 16, 2020 the Senate Select Committee on Ethics dismissed its inquiry, writing that it found no evidence her actions violated federal law, Senate rules or standards of conduct. Loeffler said third-party advisers made the trades without her knowledge.

openQuestions: Site claim that the DOJ and SEC 'closed all inquiries' into Loeffler without charges: the DOJ closure and the Senate Ethics dismissal are documented; no SEC statement was returned.
Site claim that Loeffler 'dumped $3M+ in retail while buying Citrix': coverage puts the sales at $1.2–3.1 million; the Citrix purchase was not covered by the sources returned.

The Sprecher connection relies on press references to 'her husband'; Sprecher's name and NYSE chairmanship were not in the text returned and should be confirmed from the Senate financial disclosure or a named source.
